These controls share the existing media-session setting. Turning them off also disables Bluetooth media buttons. The app’s on-screen buttons remain available. Android controls which notification and lock-screen actions it displays.

• Tap the compact music bar or swipe it up to open controls.

• Swipe the music sheet down, tap Minimize, or press Back to return to the compact bar. Music keeps playing.

• Use the seek bar or Jump to Time to move within a seekable track.

• Speed changes can preserve pitch. Equalizer settings apply only to music and are remembered.

• Sleep Timer pauses playback. A–B Repeat loops a section of the current track.

• Bookmarks remember positions per original source, including after an app restart.

• Supported headset, Bluetooth, notification and lock-screen controls use the same playback session.

• Stop ends music playback and clears its timer and A–B points.

• Playing a track from Audio creates a queue from the currently visible audio collection. Opening a single external file may create a one-track queue.

• Next and Previous move through that queue. Shuffle changes playback order; Repeat can repeat one track or the queue.

• Save Playlist stores the current queue under a unique name without modifying media files. It preserves queue order and repeated entries.

• Open You → Playlists to browse and manage saved playlists.

• Keep access to the original files. A playlist stores their locations, not copies of their audio. Temporary network playback URLs cannot be saved as durable playlists.
